A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PPTAgent and PPTEval research. Their full text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support matching content across reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original presentation-generation results, ablations, self-correction analysis, and human-evaluation correlations in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds baseline comparisons, supplementary analyses, and human-rater agreement results in Sections 4–5 and Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: The two-stage workflow, slide clustering, schema extraction, outline generation, five editing APIs, HTML representation, and self-correction procedure remain. Algorithm 1 and all 12 appendix prompts match apart from presentation changes; expanded explanations do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Zenodo10K's 10,448 presentations and evaluate with the same 50 documents and 50 reference presentations across Culture, Education, Science, Society, and Tech. Dataset statistics and sampling bounds are unchanged. The added analyses remain within this coverage.

E2.justification: V1 evaluates only the Bandyopadhyay et al. baseline, renamed DocPres in v2. V2 additionally evaluates KCTV with GPT-4o and Qwen2.5, introducing a template-based competitor alongside the retained rule-based comparator (Table 3). This substantially broadens the comparison.

E3.justification: V2 changes the stated perplexity scorer from GPT-2 to Llama-3-8B, adds ROUGE-L F1, and introduces success-rate-weighted PPTEval scores assigning zero to failed generations. The new KCTV evaluation defines success through LaTeX compilation. Existing generation configurations, task counts, and the two-retry limit remain unchanged; perplexity values across versions are therefore not directly comparable.

E4.justification: V2 adds comparative generated-slide cases (Section 5.2), score-distribution analysis (Section 5.3), and failure-weighted comparisons and ablations (Appendix C). These examine visual variation, score patterns, and the impact of failures. The original four component ablations and self-correction analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix B newly reports Fleiss' kappa for human raters: 0.61, 0.61, and 0.54, averaging 0.59. Existing human–LLM Pearson/Spearman correlations and their p-value reporting remain unchanged. Neither version documents repeated-run counts, seeds, or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: V2 adds KCTV, ROUGE-L, and failure-weighted results, revises metric correlations, and removes the ablation PPL/FID entries. Perplexities are replaced under the changed scorer; retained configurations' headline SR, FID, and PPTEval scores remain unchanged. New reporting inconsistencies include swapped DocPres/KCTV coherence attributions in Section 4.5 and GPT-4o weighted coherence of 4.20 in Table 6, whereas the stated weighting gives approximately 4.29.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(2) restate the same slide-element and editing-action formulation using collection notation instead of summations and an explicitly named edit mapping. Algorithm 1 is unchanged. No substantive theoretical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: V2 removes v1's explicit claim that PPTEval is the first comprehensive presentation-evaluation framework. The central contributions—reference-guided editing, three-dimensional evaluation, and a presentation dataset—and the overall superiority claim remain.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the limitation concerning nested-group-shape parsing with explicit dependence on reference-presentation quality; this does not establish that the parsing problem was solved. It retains generation failures and visual-design shortcomings, while adding interpretations of template constraints and failure-weighted effectiveness.

D1.justification: V2 specifies clustering placeholders and cosine similarity over ViT embeddings, and newly describes individual human ratings followed by consensus. It omits v1's eight-GPU count and explicit preprocessing-model assignments. V1's public repository link is replaced by a supplementary-materials statement promising release after review; the core prompts and APIs remain available in the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 updates the cited literature, including AutoPresent, self-correction research, and WorldCoder, while removing several earlier references. It explicitly distinguishes AutoPresent's single-slide assessment from holistic presentation evaluation. The existing rule-based/template-based positioning remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and method explanations are extensively rewritten. Detailed PPTEval criteria move to Appendix B, implementation and baselines become separate subsections, and analyses form a dedicated Section 5. Domain-level discussion moves into an expanded appendix, alongside terminology and author-list edits.

P2.justification: V2 adds score-distribution and case-study figures, an XML example, a scoring-criteria table, and weighted-results tables. V1's combined results/ablation table becomes separate Tables 3–4, and the API table moves into the main text. Self-correction plots and clustering examples are redrawn, with substantial appendix rearrangement.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's single rule-based baseline, v2's KCTV comparison, generated-slide cases, and reported human-rater agreement strengthen support for the existing claims. The principal comparison remains supported by Table 3. These gains are limited by incorrect numerical comparisons in Section 4.5, inconsistent weighted coherence in Table 6, and less direct documentation of public code/data access.
